reason: The premise that a 5 nm ALD-Al2O3 layer suppresses interdiffusion is directly supported by E2, but only up to 600 °C, not the required 1100 °C. The promise of Cr-coated Zr cladding is supported by E3 and E4, and Cr–Zr interdiffusion issues are noted in E4. However, no cited evidence supports Al2O3 stability or barrier effectiveness at 1100 °C, nor that it permits sufficient Cr outward diffusion for Cr2O3 formation, leaving key premises unsupported.
premises: A 5 nm ALD-Al2O3 layer can suppress metal interdiffusion up to 600 °C.
Cr-coated Zr-alloy cladding is a promising accident-tolerant fuel concept.
Cr–Zr interdiffusion at high temperature degrades Cr coating performance.
The Al2O3 barrier will remain effective and stable at 1100 °C in steam.
The barrier will allow sufficient outward Cr diffusion to form protective Cr2O3.
